name: renders the source-style terrain as rows before adding water
input: a height array with slopes and empty columns
test:
heights = [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 3, 4, 0, 3, 4]
expected = '+
++    +  +
+++  ++ ++
++++ ++ ++
+++++++ ++'
assert render_terrain(heights) == expected
assert heights == [5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 3, 4, 0, 3, 4]

name: renders empty and zero-height ground without water
input: Part 1 boundary cases and leading spaces
test:
assert render_terrain([]) == ''
assert render_terrain([0, 0]) == ''
assert render_terrain([0, 2, 0]) == ' +\n +'
assert render_terrain([2, 0, 2]) == '+ +\n+ +'

name: simulates a multi-drop valley and renders without trailing spaces
input: a symmetric terrain with four drops released near the left slope
test:
heights = [5, 4, 3, 1, 3, 4, 5]
expected = '+W    +
++W  ++
+++W+++
+++W+++
+++++++'
assert render_terrain(heights, 4, 1) == expected
assert heights == [5, 4, 3, 1, 3, 4, 5]

name: uses a left tie break and preserves leading blank cells
input: equal-depth reachable basins on both sides of the source

name: requires strict descent and handles an edge source
input: equal-height columns after a descent and multiple drops from the first column
test:
assert render_terrain([2, 1, 1], 1, 0) == '+W
+++'
assert render_terrain([2, 0, 2], amount=3, drop_column=0) == 'W
+W+
+W+'
assert render_terrain([], 0, 0) == ''
